record.one_liner: Cloud-based messaging platform with an HTTP Bot API for automating bots and an MTProto API for building full clients.
record.auth_notes: Bot API: static bot token from @BotFather, placed in the URL path (https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD). Not a header bearer and not OAuth. MTProto API: api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org plus user login (phone number, code, 2FA via SRP; QR and passkey also listed). I did not verify a documented OAuth flow for third-party apps, so OAuth2 is not listed.
record.access_notes: Bot token: free, via /newbot in @BotFather (the page states no fee). MTProto: free api_id at my.telegram.org with no documented approval step. The page warns of permanent bans for misuse, and accounts on unofficial clients are placed under observation.
record.blocker: A bot can only act in chats it has been added to or that have messaged it, so it cannot act as the user across their own chats. Acting as the user requires MTProto userbot access, which carries ban risk and has no OAuth. Bot rate limits: about 1 msg/s per chat, 20 msg/min per group, about 30 msg/s bulk. No official MCP server was found.

evidence.auth: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api (bot token in URL); https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather (token via /newbot); https://core.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id (api_id steps)
evidence.access: https://core.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id (free, no approval described); https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather (steps, no fee stated)
evidence.api: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api (HTTP, JSON, getUpdates and webhooks, many methods); https://core.telegram.org/api (MTProto API). I only read the first 100k of 640k characters of the Bot API page.
evidence.mcp: No official server found. The search result list was not fetched. Community example: https://github.com/sparfenyuk/mcp-telegram
